title: Model deprecation sweep controller with graceful drain and timeline recovery
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add lifecycle deprecation controller that coordinates graceful draining, replay-safe snapshotting, and timeline-based recovery for model versions. Backwards-compatible runtime behavior; configurable TTLs and safety gates.
description:
Context: Customers frequently need to retire model variants (old quantizations, interim checkpoints) without surprising production traffic. Existing rollout primitives handle promotion and canarying but lack an automated safe deprecation path for models that must be swept out of the serving fleet.
Motivation: eliminate manual deletion scripts, reduce orphaned snapshots, and provide predictable drain windows and recovery playbooks. This PR introduces a Model Deprecation Sweep Controller: design goals are safe gradual drain, snapshot-backed rollback capability during sweep, cohort-aware eviction to preserve sticky sessions, and timeline recovery for interrupted sweeps.
Key behaviors: 1) Controller understands deprecation annotations on ServeGraphs/model-versions and converts them into a staged drain plan. 2) It applies cohort-aware traffic fractions so sessions tied to older models get gradually remapped with priority for long-lived sessions. 3) Before a model node is removed, we capture a replay snapshot (lightweight KV-cache + recent-request-metadata) to support fast reinstate within the recovery window. 4) Safety gates: SLO/latency metric check, recent-error-rate threshold, and a minimum healthy instance count. 5) Config knobs: drain_window (default 10m), replay_retention (default 30m), cohort_sample_pct, fail_open boolean for emergency retention.
Implementation: adds a new controller under controllers/lifecycle with three main components: planner (generates timeboxed drain plans), coordinator (orchestrates per-pool eviction with batching and backoff), and snapshotter (compact snapshot format stored in objectstore). We extended the servegraph API surface with a deprecation_reason and deprecate_at timestamp; deprecated models are visible in the console UI and CLI.
Migration: existing ServeGraphs are unaffected until annotated.
Operator flow: 1) annotate model version and optionally set drain_window/replay_retention 2) controller schedules plan and emits events to audit-log 3) console shows per-cohort progress and allows manual pause/resume 4) if recovery invoked, controller reinstates the snapshot and resumes traffic.
Testing: unit tests for planner heuristics, e2e integration on perf-canary infra with synthetic cohorts, and chaos test that simulates controller crash-and-restart to validate timeline recovery.
Checklist: - [x] planner + coordinator implementation - [x] snapshot format + store adapter - [x] API surface and console flags - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs + playbook - [x] migration e2e on staging - [x] safety gate metric hooks - [x] confirm no default automatic deprecation (opt-in)
Commits summary: - initial planner scaffolding and tests - cohort-aware traffic allocator and sticky session support - snapshotter + compact KV dump + objectstore adapter - audit events and console wiring - safety gate integrations and smoke tests - docs + playbook and upgrade notes
Files changed (high level): controllers/lifecycle/deprecation_planner.go, controllers/lifecycle/coordinator.go, controllers/lifecycle/snapshotter.go, api/servegraph/v1alpha/model_annotations.go, console/ui/components/deprecation-panel.tsx, docs/ops/deprecation-playbook.md, integration/tests/deprecation_flow_test.go, e2e/perf-canary/simulated-cohort.yaml
Review conversation summary: - Diego Morales (2026-01-21): "Planner looks solid; we should make drain_window a cluster-level cap too so users cannot set an arbitrarily long drain that starves capacity." Author (Asha): "Ack; added cluster.level.max_drain_window config and validated with unit tests." - Riley Chen (2026-01-25): "Snapshot size might be large for some models; can we make snapshotter skip heavy KV entries and favor recent request headers?" Author: "Added retention filter and gzip+delta encoding; documented tradeoffs in snapshotter README." - Maya Kapoor (2026-01-28): "How does this interact with canary rollbacks? If a canary is promoted then deprecated quickly, we need to avoid thundering replays." Author: "Coordinator respects active rollout locks; if model is in promotion window we defer deprecation and emit a warning event to audit-log. Added integration test that simulates rapid promote->deprecate race."
CI notes: full CI passed; a flaky integration test (integration/servegraph_race_test) failed on first run and was retried; flakiness tracked in ENG-10011.
Observability: emitted telemetry for deprecation_start, deprecation_step, replay_restore, and deprecation_complete with tags (model_version, pool, cohort). Metrics guarded by feature flag.
Rollout plan: deploy controller as default off in staging, enable feature flag for select customers, run a small scheduled sweep on staging models, run two-week canary with monitoring alerts for latency and error regressions, then enable wider rollout.
Post-merge tasks: add operator guide to runbook, include deprecation metrics in console dashboards, co-ordinate with support for SUP-1420.
Merge: squash merged to main via squash and merge

Riley: Snapshotter now uses gzip+deltas and a retention filter to bound size
Maya: Coordinator respects active rollout locks to avoid race with promotions
Security: reviewed objectstore permissions and KMS usage for snapshots - approved
ci_log_summary: All checks green after retry. Build: pass, Unit: pass, Integration: pass (one flaky retried), E2E: pass on perf-canary infra. Linter: pass. Security scan: pass.
notes_for_ops: Feature is opt-in. Default retention 30m. Cluster admin can set max_drain_window. If controller fails mid-sweep, timeline recovery will resume plan from last checkpoint. Playbook located at docs/ops/deprecation-playbook.md. To force immediate rollback restore: redact deprecation annotation and call controller restore endpoint.
test_plan: Unit tests for planner heuristics; integration test that runs staged sweep on perf-canary with synthetic cohorts; chaos test that kills controller mid-sweep and verifies timeline resume; load test to validate snapshot write bandwidth under 1GB/min cap.
migration_impact: Opt-in only; no runtime behavior changed unless ServeGraph annotated. Console adds new UI components behind feature flag. Backwards compatibility maintained.
acknowledgements: Thanks to Diego, Riley, Maya, and infra team for perf runs and the sigma team for objectstore quotas review.
